locator: LE the tendency of all men who ever tried to write or talk Ethics or Religion was to run against the boundaries of language
interpretation: 'My whole tendency and I believe the tendency of all men who ever tried to write or talk Ethics or Religion was to run against the boundaries of language'; ethics 'can be no science', 'does not add to our knowledge in any sense', but 'is a document of a tendency in the human mind which I personally cannot help respecting deeply'.
attribution: The passage states that those who talk ethics or religion run against the boundaries of language, that ethics so motivated is no science and adds nothing to knowledge, and that it documents a tendency Wittgenstein deeply respects, which is the premise.
